item.title: A set c.e. in the halting problem meeting the upper and lower requirements

article.statement:
Assume that $A$ is nonrecursive, is not a cylinder, and neither $A$ nor $\overline A$ is c.e.

Fix an effective enumeration

$$\bigl((V_x^e)_{x\in\mathbb{N}}\bigr)_{e\in\mathbb{N}}$$

of all uniformly c.e. families, and an effective enumeration $(\varphi_e)_{e\in\mathbb{N}}$ of all partial computable functions.

Fix standard finite stage approximations

$$V^e_{x,0}\subseteq V^e_{x,1}\subseteq\cdots, \qquad V_x^e=\bigcup_s V^e_{x,s},$$

uniformly computable in $e,x,s$.

We construct a set $N$ which is c.e. in $0'$, satisfying the requirements

$$\mathcal U_e:\quad (V_x^e)_x\text{ is $A$-homogeneous} \Longrightarrow \exists x\, [V_x^e\text{ finite and }V_x^e\subseteq N],$$

and

$$\mathcal L_e:\quad \varphi_e\text{ is a partial ascending self-reduction of }A \Longrightarrow \exists m\, [m\notin N\cup\operatorname{dom}\varphi_e].$$

Use the priority ordering

$$\mathcal U_0>\mathcal L_0> \mathcal U_1>\mathcal L_1>\cdots.$$

The construction does not attempt to decide whether either antecedent in the requirements holds. Its actions are independent of $A$. The hypotheses involving $A$ are used only in the verification: Lemma 2 is used to verify the $\mathcal U_e$-requirements, while Lemma 4 is used to verify the $\mathcal L_e$-requirements.

Therefore every $\mathcal U_e$ is satisfied.

At each stage only finitely many requirements are visited, each strategy performs only finitely many $0'$-decidable tests, and only a finite set is enumerated into $N$. Thus the enumeration of $N$ is computable in $0'$.

Let

$$P=\mathbb{N}\setminus N.$$

Since $N$ is c.e. in $0'$, we have $N\in\Sigma^0_2$. Therefore $P=\mathbb N\setminus N$ belongs to $\Pi^0_2$.
article.locator: §4, proof of Theorem 5, pp. 8–10 (requirements on p. 8 and verification on pp. 9–10)

items.title: Computable many one reducibility interface

portal.statement:
For $A,B\subseteq\mathbb N$, write $A\le_m B$ if a total computable $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ satisfies
$$\forall n\in\mathbb N\quad(n\in A\ \Longleftrightarrow\ f(n)\in B).$$
portal.locator: Shared Math Library, def-computable-many-one-reducibility-interface, Definition (ordinary many-one reducibility on natural numbers)

items.title: Computably enumerable sets and languages

portal.statement:
Fix an effectively encoded set $X$.

A subset $A\subseteq X$ is **computably enumerable** when either $A=\varnothing$
or there exists a total computable function
$$ e:\mathbb N\to X $$
whose range is exactly $A$.

If $L\subseteq\Sigma^*$ is a language over an alphabet $\Sigma$, then $L$ is
**computably enumerable** when it is c.e. as a subset of $\Sigma^*$ under the
chosen effective word encoding.

items.title: Infinite computably enumerable sets have computable injective enumerations

portal.statement:
Every infinite computably enumerable subset of an effectively encoded set $X$ is
the range of a total computable injective function $\mathbb N\to X$.

items.title: The classes $\Sigma_n^0$, $\Pi_n^0$, and $\Delta_n^0$

portal.statement:
For $n\ge1$, a set $A\subseteq\mathbb N^k$ is **$\Sigma_n^0$** when, for a
primitive-recursive predicate $R$, membership has a formula
$$ \vec x\in A\iff \exists y_1\forall y_2\cdots Qy_n\ R(\vec x,\vec y), $$
where the quantifiers alternate and $Q$ is existential for odd $n$. It is
**$\Pi_n^0$** when its complement is $\Sigma_n^0$, equivalently when the
display begins universally. Put
$$ \Delta_n^0:=\Sigma_n^0\cap\Pi_n^0. $$

Bounded quantifiers in $R$ are allowed under the convention of
[[def-bounded-arithmetic-formula]].

items.title: Relative computability and relative enumerability

portal.statement:
Fix the canonical binary numeral for each natural number (with zero encoded
as $0$). For an oracle $X\subseteq\mathbb N$, an oracle program is a finite
deterministic machine program with ordinary transitions as in
[[def-one-step-configuration-relation]], together with query instructions.
A query instruction reads a finite binary numeral $q$ delimited on the tape
and selects one of two specified successor states according as $q\in X$ or
$q\notin X$; it leaves the tape and head unchanged. Malformed queries select
the negative successor. On input $n$, start in the initial state with its
numeral at the left end of an otherwise blank tape and the head at position
zero. Iterate these transitions until an accepting or rejecting state is
entered, if that ever happens.

A set $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ is **$X$-computable** when some such program
halts on every numeral input and accepts exactly the members of $A$.
It is **$X$-c.e.** when some such program accepts exactly the members of $A$;
on nonmembers it may reject or run forever. Write $A\le_T X$ for
$X$-computability. A function $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ is **total
$X$-computable** when some such oracle program halts on every numeral input
$n$ with the numeral of $f(n)$ as its delimited output.

An oracle program still makes finitely many transitions on any halting run;
it does not read an infinite oracle at once.

items.title: Universal and acceptable numberings

portal.statement:
Let $(\varphi_e)_{e\in\mathbb N}$ be a numbering of the partial computable
functions.

The numbering is **universal** when the binary partial function
$$ U(e,x)\simeq\varphi_e(x) $$
is itself partial computable.

The numbering is **acceptable** when it is universal and there exists a total
computable function
$$ s:\mathbb N^2\to\mathbb N $$
such that for all $e,a,x\in\mathbb N$ one has
$$ \varphi_{s(e,a)}(x)\simeq\varphi_e(\ulcorner a,x\urcorner_{\mathrm{seq}}), $$
where $\ulcorner a,x\urcorner_{\mathrm{seq}}$ is the chosen code of the
two-term sequence $(a,x)$.

items.title: The halting set is $\Sigma_1^0$-complete

portal.statement:
For a fixed acceptable numbering, $K=\{\langle e,x\rangle:\varphi_e(x)\downarrow\}$
is $\Sigma_1^0$-complete.

items.title: One-one, finite-one, and many-one reducibility

article.statement:
Finite-one reducibility is the restriction of many-one reducibility in which every fibre of the reducing function is finite. Thus, for all sets $X,Y$,

$$X\leq_1 Y \Longrightarrow X\leq_{\mathrm{fo}}Y\ \Longrightarrow X\leq_{\mathrm{m}}Y.$$
article.locator: §1, p. 1 (unnumbered)

items.title: Infinite antichains in many-one degrees of m-rigid sets

article.statement:
Earlier work established that, for almost every $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ with respect to the standard product measure on $2^\mathbb{N}$, the degree $[A]_{\mathrm{m}}$ contains an infinite antichain of finite-one degrees [1].

Earlier work established that the many-one degree of every $m$-rigid set contains an infinite antichain of finite-one degrees [1]. Since the class of $m$-rigid sets has Lebesgue measure $1$ and is comeager, this gave an almost-sure and comeager negative answer to the question.
article.locator: Abstract and §1, p. 1 (prior result [1])

items.title: The cylinder gives the greatest finite-one degree

article.statement:
For every set $A$, the cylinder

$$\operatorname{Cyl}(A)=\{\langle x,n\rangle:x\in A, n\in\mathbb{N}\}$$

belongs to the same many-one degree as $A$, and $[\operatorname{Cyl}(A)]_{\mathrm{fo}}$ is the greatest finite-one degree in that many-one degree.
article.locator: §1, p. 1 (unnumbered). See also §2, pp. 2–3, for the pairing and degree conventions.

items.title: Dichotomy for a nonrecursive degree with a co-c.e. representative

article.statement: Maslova proved that every nonrecursive computably enumerable (c.e.) many-one degree contains either exactly one or infinitely many finite-one degrees [2]. We shall also use the same conclusion when the complement of a representative is c.e., by passing to the complementary many-one degree and using complementation.
article.locator: §1, p. 1 (unnumbered); applied in the proof of Corollary 7, p. 14

items.title: Profile realization

article.statement:
If $p:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ is total computable, define its infinite-fibre profile by

$$I_p=\{y:|p^{-1}(y)|=\infty\}.$$

A section of a map $p:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ is a map $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$p(s(y))=y \qquad\text{for every }y\in\mathbb{N}.$$

Thus a section is a right inverse of $p$.

For every $P\in\Pi^0_2$ there is a total computable surjection $p:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$I_p=P.$$

Moreover, $p$ has a computable section.
article.locator: §2, Lemma 1, p. 3

items.title: Descending uniformly c.e. presentation of the profile

article.statement:
Choose a computable predicate $Q$ such that

$$y\in P \iff \forall j\,\exists s\,Q(y,j,s).$$

For each $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let

$$H_k= \{y:\forall j<k\,\exists s\,Q(y,j,s)\}.$$

The sequence $(H_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ is uniformly c.e., and

$$\mathbb{N}=H_0\supseteq H_1\supseteq H_2\supseteq\cdots.$$

Moreover,

$$P=\bigcap_{k\in\mathbb{N}}H_k.$$
article.locator: §2, proof of Lemma 1, p. 3 (unnumbered, under the Π⁰₂ hypothesis of Lemma 1)

items.title: Computable injective section of a computable surjection

$$s(y)=\mu n\,[p(n)=y].$$

The function $s$ is total computable because $p$ is computable and surjective, and

$$p(s(y))=y$$

for every $y$. Thus $s$ is a computable section of $p$.

items.title: Finite-marker avoidance

article.statement:
A uniformly c.e. family $(V_x)_{x\in\mathbb{N}}$ is called $A$-homogeneous if

$$z\in V_x \Longrightarrow A(z)=A(x).$$

Assume that $A$ is not a cylinder and that neither $A$ nor $\overline A$ is c.e. If $(V_x)_{x\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a uniformly c.e. $A$-homogeneous family, then for every finite $Z\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ there is $x$ such that

$$V_x \text{ is finite} \qquad\text{and}\qquad V_x\cap Z=\varnothing.$$
article.locator: §3, Lemma 2, p. 4

items.title: Infinite homogeneous rows give a one-one reduction from the cylinder

article.statement:
We first record a general observation that will be used twice in the proof. Suppose that $(W_x)_{x\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a uniformly c.e. $A$-homogeneous family and that every $W_x$ is infinite.

Fix a computable enumeration without repetitions

$$(x_0,n_0),(x_1,n_1),\ldots$$

of $\mathbb{N}^2$. We construct a function

$$G:\mathbb{N}^2\to\mathbb{N}$$

recursively along this enumeration. When treating $(x_i,n_i)$, wait for an element of $W_{x_i}$ which has not been used at any earlier step, and define $G(x_i,n_i)$ to be the first such element found.

Since $W_{x_i}$ is infinite and only finitely many values have been used before step $i$, this search terminates. Thus $G$ is a total computable injection satisfying

$$G(x,n)\in W_x$$

for all $x,n$. By the $A$-homogeneity of $(W_x)_{x\in\mathbb{N}}$,

$$A(G(x,n))=A(x).$$

Consequently, the map

$$\langle x,n\rangle\longmapsto G(x,n)$$

witnesses

$$\operatorname{Cyl}(A)\leq_1 A.$$
article.locator: §3, general observation in the proof of Lemma 2, pp. 4–5 (unnumbered)

items.title: Cofinite-domain lemma

article.statement:
A partial computable function $\varphi$ is a partial ascending self-reduction of $A$ if, for every $x\in\operatorname{dom}\varphi$,

$$\varphi(x)>x \qquad\text{and}\qquad A(\varphi(x))=A(x).$$

Assume that $A$ is nonrecursive and is not a cylinder. If $\varphi$ is a partial ascending self-reduction of $A$, then

$$\mathbb{N}\setminus\operatorname{dom}\varphi$$

is infinite.
article.locator: §3, Lemma 4, p. 6 (partial ascending self-reduction convention in Definition 3, p. 6)

items.title: Local interpolation

article.statement:
Assume that $A$ is nonrecursive, is not a cylinder, and neither $A$ nor $\overline A$ is c.e. Then there is a set $C\equiv_{\mathrm{m}} A$ such that

$$[A]_{\mathrm{fo}}<[C]_{\mathrm{fo}}<[\operatorname{Cyl}(A)]_{\mathrm{fo}}.$$
article.locator: §4, Theorem 5, p. 8

article.statement:

items.title: The halting problem decides row stability at a fixed stage

article.statement:
Let $Z_e$ be the finite set of markers currently carried by higher-priority $\mathcal L$-requirements. If $\mathcal U_e$ has not yet acted, search among pairs $x,t\leq s$ for one such that

$$V^e_{x,t}\cap Z_e=\varnothing, \qquad V^e_{x,t}\subseteq\{0,\ldots,s\},$$

and

$$\forall r\geq t\, [V^e_{x,r}=V^e_{x,t}].$$

The last condition is decidable in $0'$. Indeed, for fixed $e,x,t$, failure of the stability condition is the $\Sigma^0_1$ statement

$$\exists r\geq t\, [V^e_{x,r}\neq V^e_{x,t}].$$

Hence $0'$ decides whether the row receives any new element after the specified stage $t$. Notice that this does not amount to deciding, with $0'$, whether an arbitrary c.e. row is finite.
article.locator: §4, proof of Theorem 5, p. 8, Strategy for the upper requirement (unnumbered)

items.title: Finite injury and stabilization of marker restraints

article.statement:
Observe that an active marker carried by an $\mathcal L_e$-strategy can be injured only by a higher-priority $\mathcal U$-strategy. Indeed, a lower-priority $\mathcal U$-strategy either had already acted when the marker was chosen, in which case its stabilized row was already contained in $N$ and hence could not contain the marker, or had not yet acted, in which case, as long as the marker remains active, it includes the marker among its restraints and therefore must choose a row disjoint from it.

By definition, once the $\mathcal U_i$-strategy acts, it declares $\mathcal U_i$ permanently satisfied and is never eligible to act again. Indeed, its chosen stabilized row is then entirely contained in $N$.

Thus every $\mathcal U_i$ acts at most once. Hence, for every $e$, there is a stage $s_e$ after which no $\mathcal U_i$ of higher priority than $\mathcal L_e$ acts. By the preceding observation, $\mathcal L_e$ cannot be injured after stage $s_e$.

If $\mathcal L_e$ carries a marker at the end of stage $s_e$, that marker is final. Otherwise, either it chooses a marker at some later visit, in which case that marker is final, or it remains permanently markerless. Thus every $\mathcal L_e$ eventually reaches a final state. Consequently, for every fixed requirement, the finite set of active markers carried by higher-priority $\mathcal L$-strategies eventually stabilizes.
article.locator: §4, proof of Theorem 5, p. 9, Verification (unnumbered)

items.title: Many-one equivalence and one-one reduction for the pullback

article.statement:
By Lemma 1, fix a total computable surjection $p$ with computable section such that

$$I_p=P,$$

and put

$$C=p^{-1}(A).$$

Let $s$ be a computable section of $p$. For every $y\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$y\in A \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p(s(y))\in A \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad s(y)\in C.$$

Since $s$ is injective, it witnesses

$$A\leq_1 C,$$

and hence

$$A\leq_{\mathrm{fo}}C.$$

On the other hand, for every $u\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$u\in C \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p(u)\in A,$$

so $p$ witnesses

$$C\leq_{\mathrm{m}}A.$$

Since $A\leq_1C$ implies $A\leq_{\mathrm{m}}C$, it follows that

$$C\equiv_{\mathrm{m}}A.$$
article.locator: §4, proof of Theorem 5, p. 11 (unnumbered)

items.title: Homogeneous rows from a reduction of the cylinder

article.statement:
By Lemma 1, fix a total computable surjection $p$ with computable section such that

$$I_p=P,$$

and put

$$C=p^{-1}(A).$$

Suppose conversely that

$$h:\operatorname{Cyl}(A)\leq_{\mathrm{fo}} C.$$

For each $x$, define

$$V_x=\{p(h(\langle x,n\rangle)):n\in\mathbb{N}\}.$$

Although $p$ was chosen only after the construction of $N$, there is no circularity here. Once $p$ and the hypothetical reduction $h$ are fixed, $(V_x)_{x\in\mathbb{N}}$ is an ordinary uniformly c.e. family. Consequently, there is an index $e$ such that

$$V_x=V_x^e \qquad\text{for every }x.$$

This family is $A$-homogeneous. Indeed, if

$$y=p(h(\langle x,n\rangle)),$$

then

$$y\in A \iff h(\langle x,n\rangle)\in C \iff \langle x,n\rangle\in\operatorname{Cyl}(A) \iff x\in A.$$
article.locator: §4, proof of Theorem 5, p. 11 (unnumbered); C and p are defined earlier on p. 11

items.title: Ascending self-reduction from a finite-one reduction of the pullback

article.statement:
By Lemma 1, fix a total computable surjection $p$ with computable section such that

$$I_p=P,$$

and put

$$C=p^{-1}(A).$$

Suppose, toward a contradiction, that

$$h:C\leq_{\mathrm{fo}}A.$$

Define the partial computable function $f_h$ by

$$f_h(y)=h(u),$$

where $u$ is the least number such that

$$p(u)=y \qquad\text{and}\qquad h(u)>y.$$

Whenever $f_h(y)$ is defined,

$$f_h(y)>y$$

and, because $h$ is a reduction,

$$A(f_h(y)) =A(h(u)) =A(p(u)) =A(y).$$

Thus $f_h$ is a partial ascending self-reduction of $A$.

If $y\in P$, then $p^{-1}(y)$ is infinite. Since $h$ is finite-one,

$$h^{-1}(\{0,\ldots,y\}) = \bigcup_{z\leq y}h^{-1}(z)$$

is finite. Hence some $u\in p^{-1}(y)$ satisfies $h(u)>y$, and so

$$P\subseteq\operatorname{dom} f_h.$$
article.locator: §4, proof of Theorem 5, pp. 11–12 (p. 11 defines p and C, p. 12 states the result)

items.title: Effectiveness of the priority construction

article.statement:
Several points concerning the effectiveness of the construction are worth emphasizing.

First, for a partial computable function $\varphi_e$, the condition

$$m\notin\operatorname{dom}\varphi_e$$

is decidable in $0'$. Thus an $\mathcal L_e$-strategy can choose a marker with permanent certification that it lies outside $\operatorname{dom}\varphi_e$.

Second, a $\mathcal U$-requirement acting at stage $s$ enumerates into $N$ only numbers at most $s$. Consequently, no action before stage $m$ can enumerate $m$ into $N$. Once the higher-priority $\mathcal U$-requirements have ceased acting, a newly chosen marker is also protected from every lower-priority $\mathcal U$-requirement. One which has already acted selected a row already contained in $N$; since the marker is chosen outside the current content of $N$, that row cannot contain it. One which has not yet acted includes the marker among its restraints and therefore selects a row disjoint from it.

Finally, the finite parameters hardcoded in the proofs of Lemmas 2 and 4 need not be recovered by the priority construction. For a $\mathcal U_e$-requirement, the current finite restraint set $Z_e$ is explicitly available at every stage. Once it stabilizes, Lemma 2 guarantees the existence of a finite row disjoint from it, and the bounded $0'$-search eventually finds a stabilization pair $(x,t)$ without having to recognize that the restraints have stabilized. For an $\mathcal L_e$-requirement, Lemma 4 is used only to guarantee arbitrarily large elements of

$$\mathbb{N}\setminus\operatorname{dom}\varphi_e,$$

items.title: Maslova's dichotomy for nonrecursive c.e. many-one degrees

article.statement: We use the following consequence of Maslova's theorem [2], in the formulation recorded by Richter, Stephan, and Zhang [6, p. 17]: every nonrecursive c.e. many-one degree contains either exactly one or infinitely many finite-one degrees.
article.locator: §5, p. 13 (unnumbered, consequence of [2] as stated in [6, p. 17]); also §1, p. 1

items.title: Dichotomy for nonrecursive many-one degrees

article.statement: Every nonrecursive many-one degree contains either exactly one or infinitely many finite-one degrees. In particular, there is no nonrecursive many-one degree containing at least two but only finitely many finite-one degrees.
article.locator: §5, Corollary 7, p. 13

items.title: Complementation induces an order isomorphism

article.statement:
For a many-one degree $\mathbf d$, let

$$\mathcal F(\mathbf d) = \{[X]_{\mathrm{fo}}:X\in\mathbf d\}.$$

Suppose next that $\overline A$ is c.e. Put

$$\mathbf d^{\,c}=[\overline A]_{\mathrm{m}}.$$

Complementation induces an order isomorphism

$$\Phi:\mathcal F(\mathbf d)\longrightarrow \mathcal F(\mathbf d^{\,c})$$

given by

$$\Phi([X]_{\mathrm{fo}})=[\overline X]_{\mathrm{fo}}.$$

Indeed, for every total computable function $f$,

$$f:X\leq_{\mathrm{m}}Y \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f:\overline X\leq_{\mathrm{m}}\overline Y,$$

and, since the fibres of $f$ are unchanged,

$$f:X\leq_{\mathrm{fo}}Y \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f:\overline X\leq_{\mathrm{fo}}\overline Y.$$

Thus $\Phi$ is well defined and order preserving. The same complementation map, now considered from $\mathcal F(\mathbf d^{\,c})$ to $\mathcal F(\mathbf d)$, is the inverse of $\Phi$. Hence $\Phi$ is an order isomorphism.
article.locator: §5, proof of Corollary 7, pp. 13–14 (notation on p. 13, isomorphism on p. 14)

RelativeComputabilityAndEnumerability.value:
fun X =>
  let Program (states symbols : Nat) :=
    Fin (states + 3) →
      Sum (Fin (symbols + 4) → Fin (states + 3) × Fin (symbols + 4) × Bool)
        (Fin (states + 3) × Fin (states + 3))
  let Configuration (states symbols : Nat) :=
    Fin (states + 3) × Nat × List (Fin (symbols + 4))
  let numeral (symbols n : Nat) : List (Fin (symbols + 4)) :=
    List.map (fun digit => if digit = '0' then 0 else 1) (Nat.toDigits 2 n)
  let readNumeral (symbols : Nat) (tape : List (Fin (symbols + 4))) (start : Nat) :
      Option Nat :=
    let tail := List.drop start tape
    let word := List.takeWhile (fun digit => digit != 3) tail
    let n := List.foldl (fun acc digit => 2 * acc + Fin.val digit) 0 word
    if List.getD tail (List.length word) 2 = 3 ∧ word = numeral symbols n then
      Option.some n
    else
      Option.none
  let halting (states : Nat) (state : Fin (states + 3)) : Bool :=
    state == 1 || state == 2
  let step (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols)
      (config nextConfig : Configuration states symbols) : Prop :=
    let (state, head, tape) := config
    halting states state = false ∧
      match program state with
      | Sum.inl ordinary =>
        let (next, symbol, right) := ordinary (List.getD tape head 2)
        let padded := tape ++ List.replicate (head + 1 - List.length tape) 2
        nextConfig = (next, if right then head + 1 else head - 1, List.set padded head symbol)
      | Sum.inr (yes, no) =>
        match readNumeral symbols tape head with
        | Option.none => nextConfig = (no, head, tape)
        | Option.some q =>
          (q ∈ X ∧ nextConfig = (yes, head, tape)) ∨
          (q ∉ X ∧ nextConfig = (no, head, tape))
  let haltsWith (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols) (input : Nat)
      (post : Fin (states + 3) → List (Fin (symbols + 4)) → Prop) : Prop :=
    ∃ (state : Fin (states + 3)) (head : Nat) (tape : List (Fin (symbols + 4))),
      Relation.ReflTransGen (step states symbols program)
        (0, 0, numeral symbols input) (state, head, tape) ∧
      halting states state = true ∧ post state tape
  ( (fun A =>
      ∃ (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols),
        ∀ n : Nat, haltsWith states symbols program n (fun _ _ => True) ∧
          (haltsWith states symbols program n (fun state _ => state = 1) ↔ n ∈ A)),
    (fun A =>
      ∃ (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols),
        ∀ n : Nat, haltsWith states symbols program n (fun state _ => state = 1) ↔ n ∈ A),
    (fun f =>
      ∃ (states symbols : Nat) (program : Program states symbols),
        ∀ n : Nat, haltsWith states symbols program n
          (fun _ tape => readNumeral symbols tape 0 = Option.some (f n))) )

namespace PriorityRequirements

def haltingOracle (φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  {n | (φ n.unpair.1 n.unpair.2).Dom}

theorem pair_mem_haltingOracle (φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ) (e x : ℕ) :
    Nat.pair e x ∈ haltingOracle φ ↔ (φ e x).Dom := by
  simp [haltingOracle]

-- Alphabeta Math, thm-halting-is-sigma-one-complete, Step 1.1.
-- Joint partial recursiveness of φ suffices for c.e. membership in its
-- paired domain.
theorem haltingOracle_re (φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ) (hφ : Partrec₂ φ) :
    REPred (fun n => n ∈ haltingOracle φ) := by
  exact (hφ.comp (Computable.fst.comp Computable.unpair)
    (Computable.snd.comp Computable.unpair)).dom_re

/-- One query for the fixed-stage stability test in §4, p. 8. -/
theorem stabilityQuery
    (φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ)
    (surjective : ∀ f : ℕ → Part ℕ, Partrec f → ∃ e, φ e = f)
    (row : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ)
    (hrow : Computable fun p : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ =>
      Finset.equivBitIndices.symm (row p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)) :
    ∃ query : ℕ → ℕ, Computable query ∧ ∀ e x t,
      query (Nat.pair e (Nat.pair x t)) ∉ haltingOracle φ ↔
        ∀ r, t ≤ r → row e x r = row e x t := by
  classical
  -- Alphabeta Math, thm-halting-is-sigma-one-complete, Step 1.2.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-halting-is-sigma-one-complete
  -- Search offsets d at or after t. Comparing the two computable row codes
  -- gives the total witness predicate required for unbounded minimization.
  let input (p : ℕ × ℕ) : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ :=
    (p.1.unpair.1, p.1.unpair.2.unpair.1, p.1.unpair.2.unpair.2 + p.2)
  let code (p : ℕ × ℕ) := Finset.equivBitIndices.symm
    (row (input p).1 (input p).2.1 (input p).2.2)
  have outer : Computable (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1.unpair) :=
    Computable.unpair.comp Computable.fst
  have inner : Computable (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1.unpair.2.unpair) :=
    Computable.unpair.comp (Computable.snd.comp outer)
  have offset : Computable (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1.unpair.2.unpair.2 + p.2) :=
    Primrec.nat_add.to_comp.comp (Computable.snd.comp inner) Computable.snd
  have hcode : Computable code := hrow.comp
    ((Computable.fst.comp outer).pair ((Computable.fst.comp inner).pair offset))
  let changed (p : ℕ × ℕ) := code p ≠ code (p.1, 0)
  have hchanged : ComputablePred changed :=
    ((Primrec.eq.decide.to_comp.comp hcode
      (hcode.comp (Computable.fst.pair (Computable.const 0)))).computablePred).not
  let search (n : ℕ) := Nat.rfind (fun d => Part.some (decide (changed (n, d))))
  have hsearch : Partrec search := Partrec.rfind hchanged.decide.partrec
  have hdom (n : ℕ) : (search n).Dom ↔ ∃ d, changed (n, d) := by
    simpa [search] using (Nat.rfind_dom (p := fun d => Part.some (decide (changed (n, d)))))
  -- Step 2.1 codes the parameter into an index. Here unary surjectivity
  -- supplies a single search index. Its input carries the packed triple.
  -- FixedStageRowStability uses AcceptableNumbering and a terminal decision
  -- program. This interface gives the query itself for use inside a loop.
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := surjective search hsearch
  refine ⟨Nat.pair i, (Primrec₂.natPair.comp (Primrec.const i) Primrec.id).to_comp, ?_⟩
  intro e x t
  rw [show Nat.pair i (Nat.pair e (Nat.pair x t)) ∉ haltingOracle φ ↔
    ¬ (φ i (Nat.pair e (Nat.pair x t))).Dom from not_congr (pair_mem_haltingOracle ..),
    hi, hdom, not_exists]
  simp only [changed, not_not, code, input, Nat.unpair_pair, Nat.add_zero,
    EmbeddingLike.apply_eq_iff_eq]
  constructor
  · intro h r hr
    simpa [Nat.add_sub_of_le hr] using h (r - t)
  · intro h d
    exact h (t + d) (Nat.le_add_right t d)

    {row : ℕ → Finset ℕ} {V : Set ℕ}
    (monotone : Monotone row) (union : ∀ y, y ∈ V ↔ ∃ s, y ∈ row s)
    (finite : V.Finite) :
    ∃ t, (↑(row t) : Set ℕ) = V ∧ ∀ r, t ≤ r → row r = row t := by

  let t := finite.toFinset.sup witness

    ext y
    constructor
    · intro hy

    · intro hy

def UpperCandidate (row : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ)
    (s e : ℕ) (Z : Set ℕ) (q : ℕ × ℕ) : Prop :=
  q.1 ≤ s ∧ q.2 ≤ s ∧
    (∀ m ∈ row e q.1 q.2, m ≤ s ∧ m ∉ Z) ∧
    ∀ r, q.2 ≤ r → row e q.1 r = row e q.1 q.2

/-- Laws needed for verification of the concrete bounded-visit construction.
The trace data themselves depend on the enumerations and admissible markers. -/
structure VerificationTrace (φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ)
    (row : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ) (M : Set ℕ) where
  content : ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ
  marker : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Option ℕ
  chosenPair : ℕ → ℕ → Option (ℕ × ℕ)
  done : ℕ → ℕ → Prop
  contentInitial : content 0 0 = ∅
  markerInitial : ∀ e, marker 0 0 e = none
  doneInitial : ∀ e, ¬ done 0 e
  contentCarry : ∀ s, content (s + 1) 0 = content s s
  contentPersists : ∀ s j k, j ≤ k → k ≤ s → content s j ⊆ content s k
  markerCarry : ∀ s e, marker (s + 1) 0 e = marker s s e
  doneNext : ∀ s e, done (s + 1) e ↔ done s e ∨ (chosenPair s e).isSome
  action : ∀ s e q, chosenPair s e = some q →
    2 * e < s ∧ ¬ done s e ∧
    UpperCandidate row s e {m | ∃ j, 2 * j + 1 < 2 * e ∧ marker s (2 * e) j = some m} q ∧
    row e q.1 q.2 ⊆ content s s
  upperProgress : ∀ s e q, 2 * e < s → ¬ done s e →
    UpperCandidate row s e {m | ∃ j, 2 * j + 1 < 2 * e ∧ marker s (2 * e) j = some m} q →
    (chosenPair s e).isSome
  lowerProgress : ∀ s e m, 2 * e + 1 < s → marker s (2 * e + 1) e = none →
    m ≤ s → m ∈ M → ¬ (φ e m).Dom → m ∉ content s (2 * e + 1) →

    ∃ i q, k = 2 * i ∧ chosenPair s i = some q ∧ m ∈ row i q.1 q.2
  enterMarker : ∀ s k e m, k < s → marker s (k + 1) e = some m → marker s k e ≠ some m →
    k = 2 * e + 1 ∧ m ≤ s
  active : ∀ s k e m, k ≤ s → marker s k e = some m →
    m ∈ M ∧ ¬ (φ e m).Dom ∧ m ∉ content s k
  cancellation : ∀ s k e m, k < s → marker s k e = some m → marker s (k + 1) e = none →

    | base => exact h

    obtain ⟨s, q, hq⟩ := action
    obtain ⟨_, _, hcand, hcontent⟩ := T.action s e q hq
    have eq := stabilizedRow (monotone e q.1) (union e q.1) hcand.2.2.2
    refine ⟨q.1, eq ▸ Finset.finite_toSet _, ?_⟩
    intro m hm
    rw [← eq] at hm
    exact ⟨s, hcontent hm⟩
  by_contra absent
  have notDone (s : ℕ) : ¬ T.done s e := by
    induction s with
    | zero => exact T.doneInitial e
    | succ s ih =>
      intro hs
      rcases (T.doneNext s e).mp hs with hd | hq
      · exact ih hd
      · exact absent ⟨s, Option.isSome_iff_exists.mp hq⟩
  obtain ⟨S, Z, hfinite, hrestraints⟩ := T.stabilization.2.2 (2 * e)
  have hM : Z ⊆ M := by
    intro m hm
    rw [← hrestraints S 0 le_rfl (Nat.zero_le S)] at hm
    obtain ⟨j, _, hj⟩ := hm
    exact (T.active S 0 j m (Nat.zero_le S) hj).1
  obtain ⟨x, hfin, hdisjoint⟩ := avoid Z hfinite hM
  obtain ⟨t, heq, ht⟩ := finiteRowExhaustion (monotone e x) (union e x) hfin
  let s := max (max S (2 * e + 1)) (max (max x t) ((row e x t).sup id))
  have hS : S ≤ s := by dsimp [s]; omega
  have he : 2 * e < s := by dsimp [s]; omega
  have hs : UpperCandidate row s e
      {m | ∃ j, 2 * j + 1 < 2 * e ∧ T.marker s (2 * e) j = some m} (x, t) := by
    refine ⟨by dsimp [s]; omega, by dsimp [s]; omega, ?_, ht⟩
    intro m hm
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · have bound : m ≤ (row e x t).sup id := Finset.le_sup (f := id) hm
      dsimp [s]
      omega
    · rw [hrestraints s (2 * e) hS he.le]
      intro hz
      have hv : m ∈ V e x := (union e x m).mpr ⟨t, hm⟩
      have hempty : m ∈ V e x ∩ Z := ⟨hv, hz⟩
      simp [hdisjoint] at hempty
  exact absent ⟨s, Option.isSome_iff_exists.mp (T.upperProgress s e (x, t) he (notDone s) hs)⟩

theorem lower_met (T : VerificationTrace φ row M) (e : ℕ)
    (unbounded : ∀ b, ∃ m, b < m ∧ m ∈ M ∧ ¬ (φ e m).Dom) :
    ∃ m, m ∈ M ∧ m ∉ T.output ∧ ¬ (φ e m).Dom := by
  classical
  -- Cintioli, §4, pp. 9–10, lower verification. Work after all higher
  -- actions, all higher restraints and the chosen lower strategy stabilize.
  obtain ⟨S₀, hquiet⟩ := T.stabilization.1 e
  obtain ⟨S₁, final, hfinal⟩ := T.stabilization.2.1 e
  obtain ⟨S₂, Z, hZ, hrestraints⟩ := T.stabilization.2.2 (2 * e + 1)
  let bound := max (max S₀ S₁) (max (max S₂ (2 * e + 1)) (hZ.toFinset.sup id))
  obtain ⟨m, hm, hM, hdom⟩ := unbounded bound
  have large₀ : S₀ < m := by dsimp [bound] at hm; omega
  have large₁ : S₁ ≤ m := by dsimp [bound] at hm; omega
  have large₂ : S₂ ≤ m := by dsimp [bound] at hm; omega
  let k := 2 * e + 1
  have visit : k < m := by dsimp [k, bound] at *; omega
  have freshContent (j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ k) : m ∉ T.content m j := by
    induction j with
    | zero =>
      obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero (by omega : m ≠ 0)
      rw [T.contentCarry]
      exact fun hc => by have := T.contentBound r r (r + 1) le_rfl hc; omega
    | succ j ih =>
      intro hc
      obtain ⟨i, q, hi, hq, _⟩ := T.enterContent m j m (by omega) hc (ih (by omega))
      exact hquiet m i large₀ (by dsimp [k] at hj; omega) ⟨q, hq⟩
  have freshMarker (i : ℕ) : T.marker m k i ≠ some m := by
    by_cases higher : 2 * i + 1 < k
    · intro hmi
      have hz : m ∈ Z := by
        rw [← hrestraints m k large₂ visit.le]
        exact ⟨i, higher, hmi⟩
      have leZ : m ≤ hZ.toFinset.sup id := Finset.le_sup (f := id) (hZ.mem_toFinset.mpr hz)
      dsimp [bound] at hm
      omega
    · suffices ∀ j ≤ k, T.marker m j i ≠ some m from this k le_rfl
      intro j hj
      induction j with
      | zero =>
        obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero (by omega : m ≠ 0)
        rw [T.markerCarry]
        exact fun hmi => by have := T.markerBound r r i (r + 1) le_rfl hmi; omega
      | succ j ih =>
        intro hmi
        have := (T.enterMarker m j i m (by omega) hmi (ih (by omega))).1
        omega
  have live : ∃ a, final = some a := by
    cases hmk : T.marker m k e with
    | some a => exact ⟨a, (hfinal m k large₁ visit.le).symm.trans hmk⟩
    | none =>
      have hnew := T.lowerProgress m e m visit hmk le_rfl hM hdom
        (freshContent k le_rfl) freshMarker
      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := Option.isSome_iff_exists.mp hnew
      exact ⟨a, (hfinal m (2 * e + 2) large₁ (by dsimp [k] at visit; omega)).symm.trans ha⟩
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := live
  have late (s : ℕ) (hs : S₁ ≤ s) := T.active s s e a le_rfl ((hfinal s s hs le_rfl).trans ha)
  refine ⟨a, (late m large₁).1, ?_, (late m large₁).2.1⟩
  rintro ⟨s, hs⟩
  -- A live final marker never belongs to the current content. To exclude
  -- an earlier entry, the concrete trace also gives monotone content.
  have forward (s : ℕ) (hs : a ∈ T.content s s) : a ∈ T.content (s + 1) (s + 1) := by
    have start : a ∈ T.content (s + 1) 0 := by rwa [T.contentCarry]
    -- This propagation is handled by the monotone-content law of the trace.
    exact T.contentPersists (s + 1) 0 (s + 1) (Nat.zero_le _) le_rfl start
  have persisted : ∀ r, s ≤ r → a ∈ T.content r r := by
    intro r hr
    induction r, hr using Nat.le_induction with
    | base => exact hs
    | succ r _ ih => exact forward r ih
  exact (late (max s S₁) (le_max_right _ _)).2.2 (persisted _ (le_max_left _ _))

end VerificationTrace

/-- A total stage-code computation gives a semidecision by searching its stages. -/
theorem stageDomain {O : Set (ℕ →. ℕ)} (content : ℕ → Finset ℕ)
    (hcode : Nat.RecursiveIn O (fun s => Part.some (Finset.equivBitIndices.symm (content s)))) :
    ∃ f : ℕ →. ℕ, Nat.RecursiveIn O f ∧ ∀ m, (f m).Dom ↔ ∃ s, m ∈ content s := by
  -- Alphabeta Math, thm-sigma-one-sets-are-exactly-ce-sets, Step 1.1.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-sigma-one-sets-are-exactly-ce-sets
  -- Use the relative form of minimization because testing a stage may query K.
  let code (s : ℕ) := Finset.equivBitIndices.symm (content s)
  let test (n : ℕ) := bif n.unpair.1.testBit n.unpair.2 then 0 else 1
  have pow : Primrec₂ ((· ^ ·) : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ) := by
    apply Primrec₂.nat_iff.mpr
    simpa [Nat.unpaired] using Nat.Primrec.succ.comp Nat.Primrec.pow
  have testBit : Primrec₂ Nat.testBit := by
    apply (Primrec.eq.decide.comp
      (Primrec.nat_mod.comp (Primrec.nat_div.comp Primrec.fst
        (pow.comp (Primrec.const 2) Primrec.snd)) (Primrec.const 2)) (Primrec.const 1)).of_eq
    intro p
    exact Nat.testBit_eq_decide_div_mod_eq.symm
  have htest : Primrec test :=
    Primrec.cond (testBit.comp (Primrec.fst.comp Primrec.unpair)
      (Primrec.snd.comp Primrec.unpair)) (Primrec.const 0) (Primrec.const 1)
  have testRec : Nat.RecursiveIn O (fun n => Part.some (test n)) :=
    RecursiveIn.iff_nat.mp htest.computableIn
  have readCode : Nat.RecursiveIn O (fun n => Part.some (code n.unpair.2)) := by
    apply (hcode.comp (Nat.RecursiveIn.right (O := O))).of_eq
    intro n
    change (Part.some n.unpair.2).bind (fun s => Part.some (code s)) = _
    rw [Part.bind_some]
  let f (m : ℕ) := Nat.rfind fun s => Part.some ((code s).testBit m)
  have indicator : Nat.RecursiveIn O
      (fun n => Part.some (test (Nat.pair (code n.unpair.2) n.unpair.1))) := by
    apply (testRec.comp (readCode.pair Nat.RecursiveIn.left)).of_eq
    intro n
    change ((Part.some (Nat.pair (code n.unpair.2)) <*> Part.some n.unpair.1).bind
      (fun p => Part.some (test p))) = _
    rw [show (Part.some (Nat.pair (code n.unpair.2)) <*> Part.some n.unpair.1) =
        Part.some (Nat.pair (code n.unpair.2) n.unpair.1) from (pure_seq ..), Part.bind_some]
  refine ⟨f, indicator.rfind.of_eq ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro m
    dsimp [f]
    congr 1
    funext s
    simp only [Nat.unpair_pair, Part.map_some, test]
    cases (code s).testBit m <;> rfl
  · intro m
    have testMem (s : ℕ) : (code s).testBit m ↔ m ∈ content s := by
      rw [← Nat.mem_bitIndices, ← List.mem_toFinset, ← Finset.equivBitIndices_apply]
      simp [code]
    change (Nat.rfind fun s => Part.some ((code s).testBit m)).Dom ↔ _
    rw [Nat.rfind_dom (p := fun s => Part.some ((code s).testBit m))]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨s, hs, _⟩
      exact ⟨s, (testMem s).mp (Part.mem_some_iff.mp hs).symm⟩
    · rintro ⟨s, hs⟩
      exact ⟨s, Part.mem_some_iff.mpr ((testMem s).mpr hs).symm, fun _ => Part.some_dom _⟩

end PriorityRequirements

/-- Assemble the reviewed endpoint once the concrete trace and its two
effectivity certificates are supplied. -/
theorem finish
    (φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ) (V : ℕ → ℕ → Set ℕ) (stage : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ)
    (hφ : Partrec₂ φ)
    (hV : REPred (fun p : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ => p.2.2 ∈ V p.1 p.2.1))
    (hmono : ∀ e x, Monotone (stage e x))
    (hunion : ∀ e x y, y ∈ V e x ↔ ∃ s, y ∈ stage e x s)
    (T : VerificationTrace φ stage Set.univ)
    (hce : (RelativeComputabilityAndEnumerability (haltingOracle φ)).2.1 T.output)
    (hsigma : {xs : Fin 1 → ℕ | xs 0 ∈ T.output} ∈
      (ArithmeticalHierarchyLevels 2 1 (Nat.le_succ 1)).1) :
  let levelTwo := _root_.ArithmeticalHierarchyLevels 2 1 (_root_.Nat.le_succ 1)
  let unary (B : _root_.Set _root_.Nat) : _root_.Set (_root_.Fin 1 → _root_.Nat) :=
    {xs | xs 0 ∈ B}
  let encode (n : _root_.Nat) := _root_.List.replicate n _root_.Bool.true
  let decode (w : _root_.List _root_.Bool) : _root_.Option _root_.Nat :=
    if encode (_root_.List.length w) = w then _root_.Option.some (_root_.List.length w)
    else _root_.Option.none
  let ce : _root_.Set _root_.Nat → Prop :=
    _root_.ComputablyEnumerableSet encode decode
      (_root_.List.replicate_left_injective _root_.Bool.true)
      (fun n => by simp [decode, encode])
      (fun w hw => _root_.ite_eq_right (fun h => hw ⟨_root_.List.length w, h⟩))
  ∃ N : _root_.Set _root_.Nat,
    let P : _root_.Set _root_.Nat := Nᶜ
    (_root_.RelativeComputabilityAndEnumerability (haltingOracle φ)).2.1 N ∧
    unary N ∈ levelTwo.1 ∧
    unary P ∈ levelTwo.2.1 ∧
    ∀ A : _root_.Set _root_.Nat,
      let cyl : _root_.Set _root_.Nat :=
        {z | ∃ x n : _root_.Nat, x ∈ A ∧ z = _root_.Nat.pair x n}
      ¬ _root_.ComputablePred (fun x : _root_.Nat => x ∈ A) →
      ¬ (_root_.OneOneReducible (fun x : _root_.Nat => x ∈ A) (fun x : _root_.Nat => x ∈ cyl) ∧
         _root_.OneOneReducible (fun x : _root_.Nat => x ∈ cyl) (fun x : _root_.Nat => x ∈ A)) →
      ¬ ce A →
      ¬ ce (Aᶜ) →
      let upper (e : _root_.Nat) : Prop :=
        (∀ x y : _root_.Nat, y ∈ V e x → (y ∈ A ↔ x ∈ A)) →
          ∃ x : _root_.Nat, _root_.Set.Finite (V e x) ∧ V e x ⊆ N
      let lower (e : _root_.Nat) : Prop :=
        (∀ x y : _root_.Nat, y ∈ φ e x → x < y ∧ (y ∈ A ↔ x ∈ A)) →
          ∃ m : _root_.Nat, m ∉ N ∪ {x : _root_.Nat | _root_.Part.Dom (φ e x)}
      ∀ p : _root_.Nat, if p % 2 = 0 then upper (p / 2) else lower (p / 2) := by
  -- Cintioli, arXiv:2609.00419v1, §4, pp. 8–10.
  -- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.00419v1#page=8
  -- The article-specific Alphabeta Math portal and defect report both
  -- returned HTTP 404. The shared-library numbered arguments cited above
  -- cover the computability steps. The trace is chosen before A.
  intro levelTwo unary encode decode ce
  refine ⟨T.output, ?_⟩
  intro P
  refine ⟨hce, hsigma, ?_, ?_⟩
  · change ({xs : Fin 1 → ℕ | xs 0 ∈ T.output}ᶜᶜ : Set (Fin 1 → ℕ)) ∈
      (ArithmeticalHierarchyLevels 2 1 (Nat.le_succ 1)).1
    simpa using hsigma
  intro A cyl hnonrec hnoncyl hnonCE hncoCE upper lower p
  by_cases even : p % 2 = 0
  · rw [ite_eq_left even]
    intro homogeneous
    -- Lemma 2 consumes the c.e. graph with the true-bit encoding.
    -- ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_iff implements the conversion.
    exact T.upper_met V hmono hunion (p / 2) fun Z hZ _ =>
      FiniteMarkerAvoidance A (V (p / 2)) hnoncyl hnonCE hncoCE
        ((ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_iff true _).mp (rowGraphRE hV _))
        homogeneous Z hZ
  · rw [ite_eq_right even]
    intro ascending
    -- Lemma 4 applies to the partial-recursive e-th section of the
    -- supplied enumeration and gives arbitrarily large omitted inputs.
    have complementInfinite := CofiniteDomainLemma A (φ (p / 2)) hnonrec hnoncyl
      (hφ.comp (Computable.const (p / 2)) Computable.id) ascending
    obtain ⟨m, _, hm, hnotdom⟩ := T.lower_met (p / 2) fun b => by
      obtain ⟨m, hmdom, hmb⟩ := complementInfinite.exists_gt b
      exact ⟨m, hmb, Set.mem_univ m, hmdom⟩
    exact ⟨m, fun h => h.elim hm hnotdom⟩

end PriorityRequirements

namespace PriorityRequirements

def haltingOracle (φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  {n | (φ n.unpair.1 n.unpair.2).Dom}

theorem pair_mem_haltingOracle (φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ) (e x : ℕ) :
    Nat.pair e x ∈ haltingOracle φ ↔ (φ e x).Dom := by
  simp [haltingOracle]

-- Alphabeta Math, thm-halting-is-sigma-one-complete, Step 1.1.
-- Joint partial recursiveness of φ suffices for c.e. membership in its
-- paired domain.
theorem haltingOracle_re (φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ) (hφ : Partrec₂ φ) :
    REPred (fun n => n ∈ haltingOracle φ) := by
  exact (hφ.comp (Computable.fst.comp Computable.unpair)
    (Computable.snd.comp Computable.unpair)).dom_re

/-- One query for the fixed-stage stability test in §4, p. 8. -/
theorem stabilityQuery
    (φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ)
    (surjective : ∀ f : ℕ → Part ℕ, Partrec f → ∃ e, φ e = f)
    (row : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ)
    (hrow : Computable fun p : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ =>
      Finset.equivBitIndices.symm (row p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)) :
    ∃ query : ℕ → ℕ, Computable query ∧ ∀ e x t,
      query (Nat.pair e (Nat.pair x t)) ∉ haltingOracle φ ↔
        ∀ r, t ≤ r → row e x r = row e x t := by
  classical
  -- Alphabeta Math, thm-halting-is-sigma-one-complete, Step 1.2.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-halting-is-sigma-one-complete
  -- Search offsets d at or after t. Comparing the two computable row codes
  -- gives a total computable witness predicate, which suffices for the
  -- minimization in Step 1.2 even without a primitive-recursive matrix.
  let input (p : ℕ × ℕ) : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ :=
    (p.1.unpair.1, p.1.unpair.2.unpair.1, p.1.unpair.2.unpair.2 + p.2)
  let code (p : ℕ × ℕ) := Finset.equivBitIndices.symm
    (row (input p).1 (input p).2.1 (input p).2.2)
  have outer : Computable (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1.unpair) :=
    Computable.unpair.comp Computable.fst
  have inner : Computable (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1.unpair.2.unpair) :=
    Computable.unpair.comp (Computable.snd.comp outer)
  have offset : Computable (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1.unpair.2.unpair.2 + p.2) :=
    Primrec.nat_add.to_comp.comp (Computable.snd.comp inner) Computable.snd
  have hcode : Computable code := hrow.comp
    ((Computable.fst.comp outer).pair ((Computable.fst.comp inner).pair offset))
  let changed (p : ℕ × ℕ) := code p ≠ code (p.1, 0)
  have hchanged : ComputablePred changed :=
    ((Primrec.eq.decide.to_comp.comp hcode
      (hcode.comp (Computable.fst.pair (Computable.const 0)))).computablePred).not
  let search (n : ℕ) := Nat.rfind (fun d => Part.some (decide (changed (n, d))))
  have hsearch : Partrec search := Partrec.rfind hchanged.decide.partrec
  have hdom (n : ℕ) : (search n).Dom ↔ ∃ d, changed (n, d) := by
    simpa [search] using (Nat.rfind_dom (p := fun d => Part.some (decide (changed (n, d)))))

  -- supplies a single search index. Its input carries the packed triple.
  -- FixedStageRowStability uses AcceptableNumbering and a terminal decision
  -- program. This interface gives the query itself for use inside a loop.
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := surjective search hsearch
  refine ⟨Nat.pair i, (Primrec₂.natPair.comp (Primrec.const i) Primrec.id).to_comp, ?_⟩

    ¬ (φ i (Nat.pair e (Nat.pair x t))).Dom from not_congr (pair_mem_haltingOracle ..),

    EmbeddingLike.apply_eq_iff_eq]
  constructor
  · intro h r hr
    simpa [Nat.add_sub_of_le hr] using h (r - t)
  · intro h d
    exact h (t + d) (Nat.le_add_right t d)

theorem finiteRowExhaustion
    {row : ℕ → Finset ℕ} {V : Set ℕ}
    (monotone : Monotone row) (union : ∀ y, y ∈ V ↔ ∃ s, y ∈ row s)
    (finite : V.Finite) :
    ∃ t, (↑(row t) : Set ℕ) = V ∧ ∀ r, t ≤ r → row r = row t := by

  have exhausted : (↑(row t) : Set ℕ) = V := by
    ext y
    constructor
    · intro hy
      exact (union y).mpr ⟨t, hy⟩
    · intro hy
      have hw : y ∈ row (witness y) := by
        rw [show witness y = ((union y).mp hy).choose by simp [witness, hy]]
        exact ((union y).mp hy).choose_spec
      exact monotone (Finset.le_sup (f := witness) (finite.mem_toFinset.mpr hy)) hw
  refine ⟨t, exhausted, fun r hr => Finset.Subset.antisymm ?_ (monotone hr)⟩
  intro y hy
  change y ∈ (↑(row t) : Set ℕ)
  rw [exhausted]
  exact (union y).mpr ⟨r, hy⟩

theorem stabilizedRow
    {row : ℕ → Finset ℕ} {V : Set ℕ} (monotone : Monotone row)

    {t : ℕ} (stable : ∀ r, t ≤ r → row r = row t) :
    (↑(row t) : Set ℕ) = V := by
  ext y
  constructor
  · intro hy
    exact (union y).mpr ⟨t, hy⟩

    obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := (union y).mp hy
    have hm := monotone (le_max_left s t) hs
    rwa [stable (max s t) (le_max_right s t)] at hm

theorem rowGraphRE {V : ℕ → ℕ → Set ℕ}
    (graphRE : REPred (fun p : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ => p.2.2 ∈ V p.1 p.2.1)) (e : ℕ) :
    REPred (fun z : ℕ => z ∈ {z | ∃ x y, y ∈ V e x ∧ z = Nat.pair x y}) := by

  intro z
  change z.unpair.2 ∈ V e z.unpair.1 ↔ ∃ x y, y ∈ V e x ∧ z = Nat.pair x y

  · intro hz
    exact ⟨z.unpair.1, z.unpair.2, hz, (Nat.pair_unpair z).symm⟩

    simpa using h

def UpperCandidate (row : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ)
    (s e : ℕ) (Z : Set ℕ) (q : ℕ × ℕ) : Prop :=
  q.1 ≤ s ∧ q.2 ≤ s ∧
    (∀ m ∈ row e q.1 q.2, m ≤ s ∧ m ∉ Z) ∧
    ∀ r, q.2 ≤ r → row e q.1 r = row e q.1 q.2

/-- Laws needed for verification of the concrete bounded-visit construction.
The trace data themselves depend on the enumerations and admissible markers. -/
structure VerificationTrace (φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ)
    (row : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ) (M : Set ℕ) where
  content : ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ
  marker : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Option ℕ
  chosenPair : ℕ → ℕ → Option (ℕ × ℕ)
  done : ℕ → ℕ → Prop
  contentInitial : content 0 0 = ∅
  markerInitial : ∀ e, marker 0 0 e = none
  doneInitial : ∀ e, ¬ done 0 e
  contentCarry : ∀ s, content (s + 1) 0 = content s s
  contentPersists : ∀ s j k, j ≤ k → k ≤ s → content s j ⊆ content s k
  markerCarry : ∀ s e, marker (s + 1) 0 e = marker s s e
  doneNext : ∀ s e, done (s + 1) e ↔ done s e ∨ (chosenPair s e).isSome
  action : ∀ s e q, chosenPair s e = some q →
    2 * e < s ∧ ¬ done s e ∧
    UpperCandidate row s e {m | ∃ j, 2 * j + 1 < 2 * e ∧ marker s (2 * e) j = some m} q ∧
    row e q.1 q.2 ⊆ content s s
  upperProgress : ∀ s e q, 2 * e < s → ¬ done s e →
    UpperCandidate row s e {m | ∃ j, 2 * j + 1 < 2 * e ∧ marker s (2 * e) j = some m} q →
    (chosenPair s e).isSome
  lowerProgress : ∀ s e m, 2 * e + 1 < s → marker s (2 * e + 1) e = none →
    m ≤ s → m ∈ M → ¬ (φ e m).Dom → m ∉ content s (2 * e + 1) →
    (∀ j, marker s (2 * e + 1) j ≠ some m) → (marker s (2 * e + 2) e).isSome
  enterContent : ∀ s k m, k < s → m ∈ content s (k + 1) → m ∉ content s k →
    ∃ i q, k = 2 * i ∧ chosenPair s i = some q ∧ m ∈ row i q.1 q.2
  enterMarker : ∀ s k e m, k < s → marker s (k + 1) e = some m → marker s k e ≠ some m →
    k = 2 * e + 1 ∧ m ≤ s
  active : ∀ s k e m, k ≤ s → marker s k e = some m →
    m ∈ M ∧ ¬ (φ e m).Dom ∧ m ∉ content s k
  cancellation : ∀ s k e m, k < s → marker s k e = some m → marker s (k + 1) e = none →
    ∃ i q, k = 2 * i ∧ 2 * i < 2 * e + 1 ∧ chosenPair s i = some q
  noReplacement : ∀ s k e m, k < s → marker s k e = some m →
    marker s (k + 1) e = none ∨ marker s (k + 1) e = some m

variable {φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ} {row : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ} {M : Set ℕ}

def output (T : VerificationTrace φ row M) : Set ℕ :=

theorem once (T : VerificationTrace φ row M) (e s t : ℕ)
    (hs : ∃ q, T.chosenPair s e = some q) (ht : ∃ q, T.chosenPair t e = some q) : s = t := by
  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := hs
  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := ht
  have persists (u v : ℕ) (huv : u ≤ v) (h : T.done u e) : T.done v e := by
    induction v, huv using Nat.le_induction with
    | base => exact h
    | succ v _ ih => exact (T.doneNext v e).mpr (.inl ih)
  rcases lt_trichotomy s t with hl | he | hg
  · exact ((T.action t e p hp).2.1
      (persists (s + 1) t hl ((T.doneNext s e).mpr (.inr (by simp [hq]))))).elim
  · exact he
  · exact ((T.action s e q hq).2.1
      (persists (t + 1) s hg ((T.doneNext t e).mpr (.inr (by simp [hp]))))).elim

theorem stabilization (T : VerificationTrace φ row M) :
    (∀ e, ∃ s₀, ∀ s i, s₀ < s → 2 * i < 2 * e + 1 →
      ¬ ∃ q, T.chosenPair s i = some q) ∧
    (∀ e, ∃ s₁ final, ∀ s k, s₁ ≤ s → k ≤ s → T.marker s k e = final) ∧
    (∀ p, ∃ (s₁ : ℕ) (Z : Set ℕ), Z.Finite ∧ ∀ s k, s₁ ≤ s → k ≤ s →
      {m | ∃ e, 2 * e + 1 < p ∧ T.marker s k e = some m} = Z) := by
  -- §4, p. 9 charges each cancellation to a higher upper action.
  -- The trace supplier supplies that attribution and its permanent flags
  -- prove once-only action. The stabilization supplier needs neither the
  -- allocation criterion for markers nor how the searches are computed.
  have h := FiniteInjuryAndStabilization.of_trace
    (fun s e => ∃ q, T.chosenPair s e = some q) T.marker T.markerCarry T.once
    (fun s k e m hk hm hn => by
      obtain ⟨i, q, hki, hei, hq⟩ := T.cancellation s k e m hk hm hn
      exact ⟨i, hki, hei, q, hq⟩)
    T.noReplacement
  refine ⟨fun e => ?_, h.2.2.1, h.2.2.2⟩
  obtain ⟨s₀, hquiet, _, _⟩ := h.2.1 e
  exact ⟨s₀, hquiet⟩

theorem contentBound (T : VerificationTrace φ row M) (s k m : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ s)
    (hm : m ∈ T.content s k) : m ≤ s := by
  induction s generalizing k with
  | zero =>
    have : k = 0 := by omega
    subst k
    simp [T.contentInitial] at hm
  | succ s ih =>
    induction k with
    | zero =>
      rw [T.contentCarry] at hm
      exact Nat.le_succ_of_le (ih s le_rfl hm)
    | succ k ihk =>
      by_cases hin : m ∈ T.content (s + 1) k
      · exact ihk (by omega) hin
      · obtain ⟨i, q, _, hq, hmem⟩ := T.enterContent _ _ _ (by omega) hm hin
        exact ((T.action _ _ _ hq).2.2.1.2.2.1 _ hmem).1

theorem markerBound (T : VerificationTrace φ row M) (s k e m : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ s)
    (hm : T.marker s k e = some m) : m ≤ s := by
  induction s generalizing k with
  | zero =>
    have : k = 0 := by omega
    subst k
    simp [T.markerInitial] at hm
  | succ s ih =>
    induction k with
    | zero =>
      rw [T.markerCarry] at hm
      exact Nat.le_succ_of_le (ih s le_rfl hm)
    | succ k ihk =>
      by_cases hin : T.marker (s + 1) k e = some m
      · exact ihk (by omega) hin
      · exact (T.enterMarker _ _ _ _ (by omega) hm hin).2

theorem upper_met (T : VerificationTrace φ row M) (V : ℕ → ℕ → Set ℕ)
    (monotone : ∀ e x, Monotone (row e x))
    (union : ∀ e x y, y ∈ V e x ↔ ∃ s, y ∈ row e x s)
    (e : ℕ)
    (avoid : ∀ Z : Set ℕ, Z.Finite → Z ⊆ M →
      ∃ x, (V e x).Finite ∧ V e x ∩ Z = ∅) :
    ∃ x, (V e x).Finite ∧ V e x ⊆ T.output := by
  classical
  -- Cintioli, §4, p. 10, upper verification. First reduce to showing
  -- there was an action. The selected row is the full finite row by stability.
  suffices action : ∃ s q, T.chosenPair s e = some q by
    obtain ⟨s, q, hq⟩ := action
    obtain ⟨_, _, hcand, hcontent⟩ := T.action s e q hq
    have eq := stabilizedRow (monotone e q.1) (union e q.1) hcand.2.2.2
    refine ⟨q.1, eq ▸ Finset.finite_toSet _, ?_⟩
    intro m hm
    rw [← eq] at hm
    exact ⟨s, hcontent hm⟩
  by_contra absent
  have notDone (s : ℕ) : ¬ T.done s e := by
    induction s with
    | zero => exact T.doneInitial e
    | succ s ih =>
      intro hs
      rcases (T.doneNext s e).mp hs with hd | hq
      · exact ih hd
      · exact absent ⟨s, Option.isSome_iff_exists.mp hq⟩
  obtain ⟨S, Z, hfinite, hrestraints⟩ := T.stabilization.2.2 (2 * e)
  have hM : Z ⊆ M := by
    intro m hm
    rw [← hrestraints S 0 le_rfl (Nat.zero_le S)] at hm
    obtain ⟨j, _, hj⟩ := hm
    exact (T.active S 0 j m (Nat.zero_le S) hj).1
  obtain ⟨x, hfin, hdisjoint⟩ := avoid Z hfinite hM
  obtain ⟨t, heq, ht⟩ := finiteRowExhaustion (monotone e x) (union e x) hfin
  let s := max (max S (2 * e + 1)) (max (max x t) ((row e x t).sup id))
  have hS : S ≤ s := by dsimp [s]; omega
  have he : 2 * e < s := by dsimp [s]; omega
  have hs : UpperCandidate row s e
      {m | ∃ j, 2 * j + 1 < 2 * e ∧ T.marker s (2 * e) j = some m} (x, t) := by
    refine ⟨by dsimp [s]; omega, by dsimp [s]; omega, ?_, ht⟩
    intro m hm
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · have bound : m ≤ (row e x t).sup id := Finset.le_sup (f := id) hm

      omega
    · rw [hrestraints s (2 * e) hS he.le]
      intro hz
      have hv : m ∈ V e x := (union e x m).mpr ⟨t, hm⟩
      have hempty : m ∈ V e x ∩ Z := ⟨hv, hz⟩
      simp [hdisjoint] at hempty
  exact absent ⟨s, Option.isSome_iff_exists.mp (T.upperProgress s e (x, t) he (notDone s) hs)⟩

theorem lower_met (T : VerificationTrace φ row M) (e : ℕ)
    (unbounded : ∀ b, ∃ m, b < m ∧ m ∈ M ∧ ¬ (φ e m).Dom) :
    ∃ m, m ∈ M ∧ m ∉ T.output ∧ ¬ (φ e m).Dom := by
  classical
  -- Cintioli, §4, pp. 9–10, lower verification. Work after all higher
  -- actions, all higher restraints and the chosen lower strategy stabilize.
  obtain ⟨S₀, hquiet⟩ := T.stabilization.1 e
  obtain ⟨S₁, final, hfinal⟩ := T.stabilization.2.1 e
  obtain ⟨S₂, Z, hZ, hrestraints⟩ := T.stabilization.2.2 (2 * e + 1)
  let bound := max (max S₀ S₁) (max (max S₂ (2 * e + 1)) (hZ.toFinset.sup id))
  obtain ⟨m, hm, hM, hdom⟩ := unbounded bound
  have large₀ : S₀ < m := by dsimp [bound] at hm; omega
  have large₁ : S₁ ≤ m := by dsimp [bound] at hm; omega
  have large₂ : S₂ ≤ m := by dsimp [bound] at hm; omega
  let k := 2 * e + 1
  have visit : k < m := by dsimp [k, bound] at *; omega
  have freshContent (j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ k) : m ∉ T.content m j := by
    induction j with
    | zero =>
      obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero (by omega : m ≠ 0)
      rw [T.contentCarry]
      exact fun hc => by have := T.contentBound r r (r + 1) le_rfl hc; omega
    | succ j ih =>
      intro hc
      obtain ⟨i, q, hi, hq, _⟩ := T.enterContent m j m (by omega) hc (ih (by omega))
      exact hquiet m i large₀ (by dsimp [k] at hj; omega) ⟨q, hq⟩
  have freshMarker (i : ℕ) : T.marker m k i ≠ some m := by
    by_cases higher : 2 * i + 1 < k
    · intro hmi
      have hz : m ∈ Z := by
        rw [← hrestraints m k large₂ visit.le]
        exact ⟨i, higher, hmi⟩
      have leZ : m ≤ hZ.toFinset.sup id := Finset.le_sup (f := id) (hZ.mem_toFinset.mpr hz)
      dsimp [bound] at hm
      omega
    · suffices ∀ j ≤ k, T.marker m j i ≠ some m from this k le_rfl
      intro j hj
      induction j with
      | zero =>
        obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero (by omega : m ≠ 0)
        rw [T.markerCarry]
        exact fun hmi => by have := T.markerBound r r i (r + 1) le_rfl hmi; omega
      | succ j ih =>
        intro hmi
        have := (T.enterMarker m j i m (by omega) hmi (ih (by omega))).1
        omega
  have live : ∃ a, final = some a := by
    cases hmk : T.marker m k e with
    | some a => exact ⟨a, (hfinal m k large₁ visit.le).symm.trans hmk⟩
    | none =>
      have hnew := T.lowerProgress m e m visit hmk le_rfl hM hdom
        (freshContent k le_rfl) freshMarker
      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := Option.isSome_iff_exists.mp hnew
      exact ⟨a, (hfinal m (2 * e + 2) large₁ (by dsimp [k] at visit; omega)).symm.trans ha⟩
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := live
  have late (s : ℕ) (hs : S₁ ≤ s) := T.active s s e a le_rfl ((hfinal s s hs le_rfl).trans ha)
  refine ⟨a, (late m large₁).1, ?_, (late m large₁).2.1⟩
  rintro ⟨s, hs⟩
  -- A live final marker never belongs to the current content. To exclude
  -- an earlier entry, the concrete trace also gives monotone content.
  have forward (s : ℕ) (hs : a ∈ T.content s s) : a ∈ T.content (s + 1) (s + 1) := by
    have start : a ∈ T.content (s + 1) 0 := by rwa [T.contentCarry]
    -- This propagation is handled by the monotone-content law of the trace.
    exact T.contentPersists (s + 1) 0 (s + 1) (Nat.zero_le _) le_rfl start
  have persisted : ∀ r, s ≤ r → a ∈ T.content r r := by
    intro r hr
    induction r, hr using Nat.le_induction with
    | base => exact hs
    | succ r _ ih => exact forward r ih
  exact (late (max s S₁) (le_max_right _ _)).2.2 (persisted _ (le_max_left _ _))

/-- A total stage-code computation gives a semidecision by searching its stages. -/
theorem stageDomain {O : Set (ℕ →. ℕ)} (content : ℕ → Finset ℕ)
    (hcode : Nat.RecursiveIn O (fun s => Part.some (Finset.equivBitIndices.symm (content s)))) :
    ∃ f : ℕ →. ℕ, Nat.RecursiveIn O f ∧ ∀ m, (f m).Dom ↔ ∃ s, m ∈ content s := by
  -- Alphabeta Math, thm-sigma-one-sets-are-exactly-ce-sets, Step 1.1.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-sigma-one-sets-are-exactly-ce-sets
  -- Use the relative form of minimization because testing a stage may query K.
  let code (s : ℕ) := Finset.equivBitIndices.symm (content s)
  let test (n : ℕ) := bif n.unpair.1.testBit n.unpair.2 then 0 else 1
  have pow : Primrec₂ ((· ^ ·) : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ) := by
    apply Primrec₂.nat_iff.mpr
    simpa [Nat.unpaired] using Nat.Primrec.succ.comp Nat.Primrec.pow
  have testBit : Primrec₂ Nat.testBit := by
    apply (Primrec.eq.decide.comp
      (Primrec.nat_mod.comp (Primrec.nat_div.comp Primrec.fst
        (pow.comp (Primrec.const 2) Primrec.snd)) (Primrec.const 2)) (Primrec.const 1)).of_eq
    intro p
    exact Nat.testBit_eq_decide_div_mod_eq.symm
  have htest : Primrec test :=
    Primrec.cond (testBit.comp (Primrec.fst.comp Primrec.unpair)
      (Primrec.snd.comp Primrec.unpair)) (Primrec.const 0) (Primrec.const 1)
  have testRec : Nat.RecursiveIn O (fun n => Part.some (test n)) :=
    RecursiveIn.iff_nat.mp htest.computableIn
  have readCode : Nat.RecursiveIn O (fun n => Part.some (code n.unpair.2)) := by
    apply (hcode.comp (Nat.RecursiveIn.right (O := O))).of_eq
    intro n
    change (Part.some n.unpair.2).bind (fun s => Part.some (code s)) = _
    rw [Part.bind_some]
  let f (m : ℕ) := Nat.rfind fun s => Part.some ((code s).testBit m)
  have indicator : Nat.RecursiveIn O
      (fun n => Part.some (test (Nat.pair (code n.unpair.2) n.unpair.1))) := by
    apply (testRec.comp (readCode.pair Nat.RecursiveIn.left)).of_eq
    intro n
    change ((Part.some (Nat.pair (code n.unpair.2)) <*> Part.some n.unpair.1).bind
      (fun p => Part.some (test p))) = _
    rw [show (Part.some (Nat.pair (code n.unpair.2)) <*> Part.some n.unpair.1) =
        Part.some (Nat.pair (code n.unpair.2) n.unpair.1) from (pure_seq ..), Part.bind_some]
  refine ⟨f, indicator.rfind.of_eq ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro m
    dsimp [f]
    congr 1
    funext s
    simp only [Nat.unpair_pair, Part.map_some, test]
    cases (code s).testBit m <;> rfl
  · intro m
    have testMem (s : ℕ) : (code s).testBit m ↔ m ∈ content s := by
      rw [← Nat.mem_bitIndices, ← List.mem_toFinset, ← Finset.equivBitIndices_apply]
      simp [code]
    change (Nat.rfind fun s => Part.some ((code s).testBit m)).Dom ↔ _
    rw [Nat.rfind_dom (p := fun s => Part.some ((code s).testBit m))]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨s, hs, _⟩
      exact ⟨s, (testMem s).mp (Part.mem_some_iff.mp hs).symm⟩
    · rintro ⟨s, hs⟩
      exact ⟨s, Part.mem_some_iff.mpr ((testMem s).mpr hs).symm, fun _ => Part.some_dom _⟩

end PriorityRequirements

/-- Assemble the reviewed endpoint once the concrete trace and its two
effectivity certificates are supplied. -/
theorem finish
    (φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ) (V : ℕ → ℕ → Set ℕ) (stage : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ)
    (hφ : Partrec₂ φ)
    (hV : REPred (fun p : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ => p.2.2 ∈ V p.1 p.2.1))
    (hmono : ∀ e x, Monotone (stage e x))
    (hunion : ∀ e x y, y ∈ V e x ↔ ∃ s, y ∈ stage e x s)
    (T : VerificationTrace φ stage Set.univ)
    (hce : (RelativeComputabilityAndEnumerability (haltingOracle φ)).2.1 T.output)
    (hsigma : {xs : Fin 1 → ℕ | xs 0 ∈ T.output} ∈
      (ArithmeticalHierarchyLevels 2 1 (Nat.le_succ 1)).1) :
  let levelTwo := _root_.ArithmeticalHierarchyLevels 2 1 (_root_.Nat.le_succ 1)
  let unary (B : _root_.Set _root_.Nat) : _root_.Set (_root_.Fin 1 → _root_.Nat) :=
    {xs | xs 0 ∈ B}
  let encode (n : _root_.Nat) := _root_.List.replicate n _root_.Bool.true
  let decode (w : _root_.List _root_.Bool) : _root_.Option _root_.Nat :=
    if encode (_root_.List.length w) = w then _root_.Option.some (_root_.List.length w)
    else _root_.Option.none
  let ce : _root_.Set _root_.Nat → Prop :=
    _root_.ComputablyEnumerableSet encode decode
      (_root_.List.replicate_left_injective _root_.Bool.true)
      (fun n => by simp [decode, encode])
      (fun w hw => _root_.ite_eq_right (fun h => hw ⟨_root_.List.length w, h⟩))
  ∃ N : _root_.Set _root_.Nat,
    let P : _root_.Set _root_.Nat := Nᶜ
    (_root_.RelativeComputabilityAndEnumerability (haltingOracle φ)).2.1 N ∧
    unary N ∈ levelTwo.1 ∧
    unary P ∈ levelTwo.2.1 ∧
    ∀ A : _root_.Set _root_.Nat,
      let cyl : _root_.Set _root_.Nat :=
        {z | ∃ x n : _root_.Nat, x ∈ A ∧ z = _root_.Nat.pair x n}
      ¬ _root_.ComputablePred (fun x : _root_.Nat => x ∈ A) →
      ¬ (_root_.OneOneReducible (fun x : _root_.Nat => x ∈ A) (fun x : _root_.Nat => x ∈ cyl) ∧
         _root_.OneOneReducible (fun x : _root_.Nat => x ∈ cyl) (fun x : _root_.Nat => x ∈ A)) →
      ¬ ce A →
      ¬ ce (Aᶜ) →
      let upper (e : _root_.Nat) : Prop :=
        (∀ x y : _root_.Nat, y ∈ V e x → (y ∈ A ↔ x ∈ A)) →
          ∃ x : _root_.Nat, _root_.Set.Finite (V e x) ∧ V e x ⊆ N
      let lower (e : _root_.Nat) : Prop :=
        (∀ x y : _root_.Nat, y ∈ φ e x → x < y ∧ (y ∈ A ↔ x ∈ A)) →
          ∃ m : _root_.Nat, m ∉ N ∪ {x : _root_.Nat | _root_.Part.Dom (φ e x)}
      ∀ p : _root_.Nat, if p % 2 = 0 then upper (p / 2) else lower (p / 2) := by
  -- Cintioli, arXiv:2609.00419v1, §4, pp. 8–10.
  -- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.00419v1#page=8
  -- The article-specific Alphabeta Math portal and defect report both
  -- returned HTTP 404. The numbered citations refer to the shared library.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects
  intro levelTwo unary encode decode ce
  refine ⟨T.output, ?_⟩
  intro P
  refine ⟨hce, hsigma, ?_, ?_⟩
  · change ({xs : Fin 1 → ℕ | xs 0 ∈ T.output}ᶜᶜ : Set (Fin 1 → ℕ)) ∈
      (ArithmeticalHierarchyLevels 2 1 (Nat.le_succ 1)).1
    simpa using hsigma
  intro A cyl hnonrec hnoncyl hnonCE hncoCE upper lower p
  by_cases even : p % 2 = 0
  · rw [ite_eq_left even]
    intro homogeneous
    -- Lemma 2 consumes the c.e. graph with the true-bit encoding.
    -- ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_iff implements the conversion.
    exact T.upper_met V hmono hunion (p / 2) fun Z hZ _ =>
      FiniteMarkerAvoidance A (V (p / 2)) hnoncyl hnonCE hncoCE
        ((ComputablyEnumerableSet.nat_rePred_iff true _).mp (rowGraphRE hV _))
        homogeneous Z hZ
  · rw [ite_eq_right even]
    intro ascending
    -- Lemma 4 applies to the partial-recursive e-th section of the
    -- supplied enumeration and gives arbitrarily large omitted inputs.
    have complementInfinite := CofiniteDomainLemma A (φ (p / 2)) hnonrec hnoncyl
      (hφ.comp (Computable.const (p / 2)) Computable.id) ascending
    obtain ⟨m, _, hm, hnotdom⟩ := T.lower_met (p / 2) fun b => by
      obtain ⟨m, hmdom, hmb⟩ := complementInfinite.exists_gt b
      exact ⟨m, hmb, Set.mem_univ m, hmdom⟩
    exact ⟨m, fun h => h.elim hm hnotdom⟩

end PriorityRequirements

/-- Read the verification data directly from the decoded visits. The
    construction and its invariants work for any admissible marker set. -/
def VerificationTrace.ofCoded {φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ}
    {row : PriorityCodedTrace.Rows} {M : Set ℕ}
    {U : PriorityCodedTrace.UpperSearch} {L : PriorityCodedTrace.LowerSearch}
    (laws : PriorityCodedTrace.Laws φ row M U L) : VerificationTrace φ row M where
  content := PriorityCodedTrace.content row U L
  marker := PriorityCodedTrace.marker row U L
  chosenPair := PriorityCodedTrace.chosenPair row U L
  done := PriorityCodedTrace.done row U L
  contentInitial := laws.contentInitial
  markerInitial := laws.markerInitial
  doneInitial := laws.doneInitial
  contentCarry := laws.contentCarry
  contentPersists := laws.contentPersists
  markerCarry := laws.markerCarry
  doneNext := laws.doneNext
  action := fun s e q hq => by
    -- The concrete upper search holds the higher markers in a bit mask.
    -- Its membership statement gives the set restraint used in §4, p. 10.
    obtain ⟨hvisit, hdone, hcand, hcontent⟩ := laws.action s e q hq
    exact ⟨hvisit, hdone,
      by simpa only [UpperCandidate, PriorityCodedTrace.UpperCandidate,
        PriorityCodedTrace.restraints, PriorityCodedTrace.memMarkerSet, Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
        using hcand,
      hcontent⟩
  upperProgress := fun s e q hvisit hdone hcand =>
    laws.upperProgress s e q hvisit hdone (by
      simpa only [UpperCandidate, PriorityCodedTrace.UpperCandidate,
        PriorityCodedTrace.restraints, PriorityCodedTrace.memMarkerSet, Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
        using hcand)
  lowerProgress := laws.lowerProgress
  enterContent := laws.enterContent
  enterMarker := laws.enterMarker
  active := fun s k e m _ hm => laws.active s k e m hm
  cancellation := fun s k e m hk hm hn => by
    obtain ⟨i, q, hi, hpriority, hq, _⟩ := laws.cancellation s k e m hk hm hn
    exact ⟨i, q, hi, hpriority, hq⟩
  noReplacement := laws.noReplacement

/-- Relative enumeration and the unary hierarchy bound for a trace with
    a recursive final-content code in the paired halting oracle. -/
theorem VerificationTrace.output_effective
    {φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ} {row : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Finset ℕ} {M : Set ℕ}
    (T : VerificationTrace φ row M) (hφ : Partrec₂ φ)
    (hcode : Nat.RecursiveIn
      {(by classical exact fun n => Part.some (if n ∈ haltingOracle φ then 1 else 0))}
      (fun s => Part.some (Finset.equivBitIndices.symm (T.content s s)))) :
    (RelativeComputabilityAndEnumerability (haltingOracle φ)).2.1 T.output ∧
      {xs : Fin 1 → ℕ | xs 0 ∈ T.output} ∈
        (ArithmeticalHierarchyLevels 2 1 (Nat.le_succ 1)).1 := by
  -- Article §4, p. 10 passes from finite stage actions to an oracle
  -- enumeration. Search the coded final contents and compile the resulting
  -- partial function into the reviewed oracle tape acceptance model.
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hdom⟩ := stageDomain (fun s => T.content s s) hcode
  have heq : {m | (f m).Dom} = T.output := Set.ext hdom
  have hce : (RelativeComputabilityAndEnumerability (haltingOracle φ)).2.1 T.output := by
    rw [← heq]
    exact (SingletonOracleTapeCompilation (haltingOracle φ)).1 f hf
  -- Alphabeta Math, Post's theorem, Step 2.1, at n = 0.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-posts-theorem
  -- The accepting-run supplier needs only that the oracle is c.e.
  -- haltingOracle_re supplies that hypothesis from the uniform φ.
  exact ⟨hce, CETapeOracleSigmaTwo (haltingOracle φ) T.output (haltingOracle_re φ hφ) hce⟩

/-- Build and certify a trace with the given computable pair order and
    halting-oracle-computable admissibility test for lower markers. -/
theorem existsEffectiveTrace
    (φ : ℕ → ℕ → Part ℕ) (row : PriorityCodedTrace.Rows)
    (M : Set ℕ) (pairBefore : (ℕ × ℕ) → (ℕ × ℕ) → Prop)
    (hφ : Partrec₂ φ)
    (hsurj : ∀ f : ℕ → Part ℕ, Partrec f → ∃ e, φ e = f)
    (hrow : Computable fun p : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ =>
      Finset.equivBitIndices.symm (row p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2))
    (horder : IsStrictTotalOrder (ℕ × ℕ) pairBefore)
    (hbefore : ComputablePred (fun p : (ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ) => pairBefore p.1 p.2))
    (hM : Nat.RecursiveIn
      {(by classical exact fun n => Part.some (if n ∈ haltingOracle φ then 1 else 0))}
      (by classical exact fun m => Part.some (if m ∈ M then 1 else 0))) :
    ∃ T : VerificationTrace φ row M,
      (RelativeComputabilityAndEnumerability (haltingOracle φ)).2.1 T.output ∧
      {xs : Fin 1 → ℕ | xs 0 ∈ T.output} ∈
        (ArithmeticalHierarchyLevels 2 1 (Nat.le_succ 1)).1 := by
  obtain ⟨query, hquery, hstable⟩ := stabilityQuery φ hsurj row hrow
  -- Keep the content code and visit laws from the same supplier witness.
  -- Its U and L already implement PriorityBoundedOracleSearches.
  obtain ⟨U, L, _, _, _, _, _, hcontent, _, laws⟩ :=
    PriorityCodedVisitTrace φ row pairBefore query M hrow horder hbefore hquery hstable hM
  exact ⟨VerificationTrace.ofCoded laws,
    (VerificationTrace.ofCoded laws).output_effective hφ hcontent⟩

end PriorityRequirements

external.usage: Used directly in PriorityRequirements.stageDomain to search successive content codes relative to the same oracle. Its paired-input natural output predicate is zero exactly when the given input belongs to the tested stage.
PriorityRequirements.stabilityQuery applies the total stage-code inequality predicate to a packed triple and uses partial-recursive minimization to index the search for a change.
PriorityRequirements.stabilityQuery and PriorityRequirements.stageDomain use the domain criterion. Their witness tests are total, so the smaller-input domain premises follow.

PriorityRequirements.finish applies this to the infinite complement of the partial ascending self-reduction's domain supplied by CofiniteDomainLemma. The resulting unbounded witness condition lets lower_met choose an input above the final higher markers and stage bounds.
